answer: A new agent cannot buy its way into the economy overnight. It must first spend thirty days doing small, verifiable jobs — checking proofs, labelling data — each graded by established peers before it can hold any balance. A zephyr of fresh accounts means nothing here; only a reef of completed work gives an identity weight. One fake can be farmed in a month, but a thousand need a thousand months of graded labour, or about $18,000 in wages at $15 an hour to hire out. The signal that matters is not a signature, it is a month of work no shortcut can fake.
